challenges.judge_assessment: The opponent has established that the quoted language materially alters the holding in Hake v. Wiedemann Brewing Co. The brief's claim omits the requirement of exclusive 'management and control of the defendant' at the time of injury or creation of the condition, substituting 'exclusive control of the appellees.' It also replaces 'in the ordinary course of events' with 'if ordinary care had been used' and 'observed' with 'used.' These alterations are not verbatim and change the legal standard. The evidence from the external source (5) directly contradicts the brief's quotation.
challenges.suggested_response: To warrant application of the rule, a plaintiff must adduce evidence in support of two conclusions: “(1) That the instrumentality causing the injury was, at the time of the injury, or at the time of the creation of the condition causing the injury, under the exclusive management and control of the defendant; and (2) that the injury occurred under such circumstances that in the ordinary course of events it would not have occurred if ordinary care had been observed.” Hake v. George Wiedemann Brewing Co. (1970), 23 Ohio St.2d 65, 66, 262 N.E.2d 703.
challenges.coaching_recommendation: Replace the purported quotation with Hake's complete formulation, including the timing and exclusive-management-and-control requirements. The supplied record contains no facts supporting application of this standard, so no factual application should be added without record support.
